To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

journalists in a regional newspaper in the North of England were observed to have radically revised their perceptions of Web technology, and to have reversed their policies on Web practices, in the period 2006 to 2011.
journalists’ perceptions of Web technologies were fluid and contradictory, and that their professional imagination was shaped by the parent print culture.

the journalists at the Northern Echo newspaper in Britain revised their opinions of the optimum web practice and sometimes reversed policies in the five years between 2006 and 2011, and that they were observed to have been strongly influenced by their parent print culture and routines despite pioneering a new partnership with an independent TV company.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the ways in which journalists perceive and use digital technologies, and the ways in which they are affected by them.
the ways in which a regional newspaper has responded to a changing media landscape.
the role of the journalist in the digital age, and the extent to which they can be seen as the agents of change.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Northern Echo newspaper was a ‘slow adopter’ of Web technologies, with a strong emphasis on print values.
, in a period of technological evolution, the Northern Echo newspaper was in a state of constant revision of its own identity.
the Web is not a siren song for journalists, but neither a path to salvation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

, although journalists are often perceived as resistant to change, they are not always resistant to the same change, and their views can shift over time, and that the ‘professional imagination’, as well as the ‘professional project’, is a powerful factor in the adoption and rejection of new technologies and practices.
the newspaper’s Web presence is not an extension of print, but rather a separate entity, which has its own rules, and which is not necessarily subordinate to its parent.

the study shows the importance of understanding the local context of technological change, the role of the ‘professional imagination’, and the need for a more nuanced understanding of how technology can be used to enhance journalism.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ‘digital’ in digital journalism is not a single entity but a series of interlinked, evolving technologies that have different implications for the newsroom and for news production.
, despite the rapid evolution of Web technologies, the journalists’ perceptions of the Web remained remarkably consistent.
the professional imagination of a regional newspaper can be a complex, contradictory, and often unpredictable phenomenon.
